changelog: [When to Segment]: refined the -고 bullet so the boundary is moved past the point where a governed object/complement appears (rather than omitted), instead of just noting 'otherwise wait'.

[When to Segment]: refined the -는데 bullet so that when the following clause is an explicit contrast or a rhetorical question's answer, the boundary is moved to AFTER that contrasting/answering clause rather than cut right after -는데.
[When to Segment]: refined the -니까 bullet to keep chained causal connectives (-니까...-어서...) together and place the single boundary only at the final connector before the outcome clause.

[When to Segment]: added a permissive rule to split right after a sentence-initial discourse marker/topic-time adverbial (근데, 그래서, 그러면, 그럼, 그럼 이제, 이번에는) followed by a complete independent clause, explicitly even when a later boundary already exists in the same sentence — this recovers free latency gains shown by missed_gain evidence.
[When to Segment]: added a permissive rule to split right before a trailing opinion/nominalizer tail (-는 거 같아/같애, -는 것 같다) when the preceding clause is already complete.

[When to Segment]: added a rule to keep a rhetorical question and its immediately following short confirmation token (네, 어, 맞아) together, moving the boundary to after the confirmation token instead of before it.

[Decision Procedure]: updated step 1 so that when A's verb needs a later object, A is part of an unresolved causal chain, A is a -는데 clause awaiting its contrast/answer, or A is a rhetorical question followed only by a short confirmation, the boundary is not simply rejected but MOVED further into B past the resolution point and re-checked, instead of leaving the sentence unsplit.
